title: Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) � Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS) Prototype
description: The purpose of this update is to publish the Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) for the Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS) Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP). Please review the attached document titled "AWS_RPP_Official_QandA" for the Government's responses to all received industry questions. As confirmed in the Q&A, the deadline for proposal submissions remains 01 October 2026 at 16:00 Eastern Time (ET). All other terms, requirements, and submission instructions in the solicitation remain unchanged. 1.0 Overview The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC), on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground, Project Manager Maneuver Medical Systems (PM M2S), is issuing this Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) to solicit prototype project proposals for a modernized Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS). This RPP is issued pursuant to the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 4022. This is a DIRECT OTA and is NOT a solicitation for a procurement contract under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Consortium membership is not required to respond to this RPP. 2.0 Mission Need & Scope The U.S. Army requires a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Non-Developmental Item (NDI) anesthesia workstation system capable of supporting life-saving medical operations in austere environments at Role of Care (ROC) 3 with little to no modification. The system must overcome the capability gaps of legacy systems, specifically regarding interoperability with Army Oxygen Generation Systems, heavy logistical footprint (weight), and proprietary maintenance constraints. The Government intends to award one (1) OT Agreement for the delivery of two (2) prototype units. These units will undergo rigorous operational testing by the Medical Test and Evaluation Activity (MTEAC) and environmental testing conducted in accordance with MIL-STD-810H. Proposed solutions must be FDA-cleared for human use and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant. A high priority for this effort is organic supportability. The Government strongly prefers systems designed to be maintainable by military Biomedical Equipment Technicians (BMETs) at the Field and Depot levels without reliance on proprietary vendor service contracts. 3.0 Follow-On Production Authority In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f), this OT Agreement is issued with a provision for follow-on production. Upon successful prototype completion and validation, the Government may award a follow-on production contract or OT Agreement for approximately one hundred and eighty (180) AWS units without further competitive procedures. 4.0 Proposal Submission Instructions All proposal instructions, technical specifications (CODS and APAs), and evaluation criteria are detailed in the attached Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) document. Questions: All questions must be submitted in writing via email to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialist no later than 15:00 ET on 17 September 2026. Proposals: Proposals must be submitted via DoD SAFE file transfer or secure email no later than 16:00 ET on 01 October 2026. Communications: Unauthorized contact with program office personnel or technical end-users regarding this RPP may result in disqualification. All communications must be directed to the points of contact listed below. description: Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia mammografiatutkimuspalveluista lausuntoineen Lapin hyvinvointialueen ja Työterveys Lappica Oy:n tarpeisiin. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen (2) osa-alueeseen, joista tarjoaja voi jättää tarjouksen joko yhteen tai molempiin: 1. Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen Rovaniemellä: Palvelu tuotetaan Palveluntuottajan toimitiloissa Rovaniemellä. 2. Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen Kemijärvellä: Palvelu tuotetaan Tilaajan toimitiloissa Kemijärvellä Tilaajan laitteilla. Kummallekin osa-alueelle valitaan yksi (1) Palveluntuottaja. Palveluntuottajan tulee sitoutua tuottamaan palvelu kokonaisuudessaan tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankittavien palvelujen tarkempi sisältö ja sitä koskevat ehdottomat vaatimukset on kuvattu liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus ja ehdottomat vaatimukset. Palvelukuvauksessa esitetyt hankintamäärät ovat arvioita, joiden mukaiseen palvelutuotantoon tarjoajalla tulee olla valmius sopimuskauden ja mahdollisten optiokausien aikana. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin, vaan hankinnan määrä riippuu tarpeesta. Hankinnalla täydennetään Tilaajan omaa palvelutuotantoa. Palvelutuotannon suunniteltu aloitusajankohta Rovaniemellä on 1.12.2026 ja Kemijärvellä 1.2.2027. Kyseessä on julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista annetun lain (1397/2016) 25 §:n 1 momentin 3 kohdan mukainen kansallisen kynnysarvon ylittävä liitteen E mukainen sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluhankinta. Hankinnan kohteena ovat mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen. Hankittavan palvelun sisältö ja arviot hankittavista tutkimuksista lausuntoineen vuositasolla Rovaniemellä, on ilmoitettu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus ja ehdottomat vaatimukset. Hankintasopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta, vaan palveluja hankitaan Tilaaja kulloisenkin tarpeen mukaan., Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen Kemijärvellä Tutkimukset tuotetaan Kemijärvellä Tilaajan toimitiloissa ja Tilaajan laitteilla. Hankittavien palvelujen sisältö ja arviot hankittavista tutkimuksista lausuntoineen Kemijärvellä vuositasolla, on ilmoitettu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus ja ehdottomat vaatimukset. title: Northrop Grumman, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) intends to negotiate and award a sole source, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC), CAGE Code 70974, of Melbourne, FL, for the procurement of supplies and services required for the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye (AHE) Block II retrofit program. This effort encompasses the procurement, storage, assembly, and delivery of up to one hundred (100) E-2D Block II retrofit kits; installation and modification services for up to eighty-three (83) fleet E-2D AHE aircraft; procurement of Long-Lead Material (LLM); non-recurring engineering (NRE) and integration support; Manufacturing Readiness Assessments (MRAs); First Article Inspections (FAIs); depot-level and in-service repair and maintenance services, including restoring Not Ready For Issue (NRFI) components to Ready For Issue (RFI) condition; Over and Above (O&A) work; sustaining engineering; and integrated logistics and supply support. Operational verification and checkouts shall be conducted utilizing U.S. Navy Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETMs), and post-modification Functional Check Flights (FCFs) shall be conducted in accordance with Naval Air Training and Operating Procedures Standardization (NATOPS) publications in support of the E-2/C-2 Airborne Command and Control Systems Program Office (PMA-231). A sole source acquisition will be procured under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye aircraft, including the Hawkeye Cockpit Tech Refresh (HECTR) and Theater Combat ID (TCID) Block II configurations developed under preceding development contract N00019-23-F-2625. NGSC is the only known qualified, responsible source that possesses the requisite technical expertise, manufacturing infrastructure, specialized tooling, and proprietary technical data and software source code required to fulfill these requirements without causing unacceptable operational delays to fleet Planned Maintenance Intervals (PMIs) and substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Northrop Grumman Corporation. Unless otherwise stated herein, no additional written information is available. Requests for the same will be disregarded.

description: This is a combined Sources Sought/Request for Information (RFI) notice. Any information submitted by respondents to this request is strictly voluntary. All information received from this Sources Sought/RFI notice will be used for planning and market research purposes only. The United States (U.S.) Government will treat your response to this Sources Sought/RFI notice as information. Based on the review of responses to this Sources Sought/RFI notice, the Government may elect to release a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) at a future date. The Period of Performance (PoP) for any subsequent contract effort will remain variable and dependent upon the maturity and deployment timelines of the offered solutions. Under any future resultant contract, the prime contractor will be required to execute a comprehensive modernization effort, to include the delivery of all required radar equipment, provision of initial spares, and the execution of all necessary site modifications and system integration. 3.0 Desired Capabilities The below capabilities integrate specific parameters required by the Brazilian Air Force. 3.1 General System must demonstrate the capability to achieve full flight inspection certification (FAA/ICAO standards) for both Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) and Precision Approach Radar (PAR) functions. 3.2 Transportation a. Threshold (T): Setup within 8 hours by 4 personnel. Transportable by KC-390 aircraft. b. Objective (O): Setup within 4 hours by 2 personnel. Roll-on/Roll-off capable on KC-390 with zero major disassembly. 3.3 Equipment Specifics 3.3.1 Surveillance a. Primary Surveillance Radar (PSR) Range & Altitude Threshold (T): Minimum range of 30 NM. (O): 90% or higher for a 2m2 target. c. Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) Range & Altitude (T): Minimum range of 60 NM and altitude coverage up to 18,000 ft AGL. (O): Range of 100 NM and altitude coverage up to 35,000 ft AGL. d. SSR Modes & Capability (T): Must support ATCRBS, Modes 3/A, C, S, and ADS-B. (O): Full support for all Threshold modes plus native cryptographic integration for secure military Mode 5 e. SSR Probability of Detection (Pd) (T): 90% or higher. (O): 95% or higher. 3.3.2 Precision Landing a. PAR Coverage & Switch Time (T): Service up to 6 runways, switchable within 60 seconds. (O): Service > 6 runways, switchable in under 30 seconds. b. PAR Instrumented Range (T): Reliable azimuth/elevation tracking and detection out to a minimum range of 10 NM. (O): Reliable azimuth/elevation tracking and detection out to 20 NM or greater. c. PAR Target Capacity (T): Track up to 50 aircraft in azimuth and 22 aircraft in elevation. (O): Track over 100 combined aircraft simultaneously. d. PAR Detection Probability (2m� target) (T): 90% probability at 10 NM. (O): 95% probability at 15 NM in rain and 20 NM in clear weather. e. PAR Resolution (T): Range: 400 ft, Azimuth: 1.2 degrees, Elevation: 0.6 degrees (all with greater than or equal to 80% probability). (O): Margins improved by 20% over threshold values. f. PAR Accuracy (T): Range: less than or equal to �100 ft (or 2%). Azimuth: less than or equal to �30 ft. Elevation: less than or equal �20 ft. (O): Margins improved by 20% over threshold values. 3.3.3 Communications Data Interoperability (T=O): Output standard ASTERIX Eurocontrol data format for all surveillance outputs. ATC Positions, Display, & Automation (T): Two (2) ATC positions. Explain and provide detailed documentation of the proposed a. ATC automation/display system. (O): Fully modular system expandable up to six (6) ATC positions. ATC Radio Communications (T): Each ATC position must have UHF/VHF transmit/receive capability and the ability to simultaneously monitor UHF/VHF Guard frequencies. (O): Fully integrated voice switch system with secure, encrypted transmit/receive capability. 3.3.4 System Reliability & Redundancy (T=O): Backup PSR transmitter or redundancy in the system is required. Backup power (UPS) is required. Mean Time Between Critical Failure (MTBCF) > 2,000 hours. 3.3.5 Maintainability (MTTR) (T): Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) < 30 minutes. (O): Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) < 15 minutes. 3.3.6 System Operational Certifications Identify whether or not the system has any/all of six (6) certifications for operations in both CONUS and OCONUS: Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS) Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) Mark XII System (AIMS); Cybersecurity; Interoperability and Supportability (I&S); National Airspace System (NAS); Spectrum; and Transportability (air, ground and sea). 3.3.7 Ancillary & Support Equipment Requirements (T): Identify all generators, environmental control unit (ECU), hardware/software, and ancillary equipment requirements necessary to support standalone system operations. (O): Offer integrated, self-contained auxiliary systems that minimize external logistics footprint and setup time. 3.4 Maintenance Capabilities a. title: Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility Services AE IDIQ, Unrestricted
description: THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED PROCUREMENT. This procurement will result in one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for multi-discipline Architect-Engineer (A-E) services for Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility services at various Navy and Marine Corps installations primarily in the Navy Region Southwest but may also include work worldwide. These services will be procured in accordance with 40 USC Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers, as implemented by FAR 36. The IDIQ contract will be for a base period of two (2) years and three (3) one-year option periods (if exercised). The total fee for the contract term shall not exceed $30,000,000. The guaranteed minimum for the contract term (including option years) is $1,000. Firm-fixed price task orders will be negotiated for this contract. The minimum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $25,000. The maximum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $2,500,000. There will be no dollar limit per year. Estimated start date is March 2027. The Small Business size standard classification is North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330 (Engineering Services). The Government seeks the most highly qualified firm to perform the required services, based on the demonstrated competence and qualifications, in accordance with the selection criteria. Primary A-E Services: 1. Land Use Planning. 2. Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (AICUZ) and Range Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (RAICUZ) Studies. 3. Encroachment Action Plans (EAP) or Encroachment Control Plans (ECP). 4. Strategic Engagement and Communication Plans (SECP). 5. Outreach Planning Materials. 6. Electronic Database. Secondary Services: 1. Other related studies/analysis: Provide additional services to assist in implementation of encroachment management studies, Range Complex Management Plans (RCMP), Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMP), Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program plans, and other special planning, engineering, and encroachment support deliverables, such as analytical assessments, geospatial analysis and simulations, traffic studies, glint/glare analysis, radar assessments, plume analysis and modeling, lighting studies, and socio-economic studies. 2. Other Related Reports or Documentation: Deliverables also include assistance with incidental services related to providing public notice for studies and publicizing and providing training on encroachment-related studies. title: 58--OLES LONG RANGE MWIR THERMAL BINOCULARS
description: The Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management (BLM), intends to award a sole-source contract to Teledyne FLIR for three Recon HD high-definition, dual-sensor long-range thermal binocular/camera systems with 2� doubler lenses. BLM Law Enforcement currently utilizes legacy Teledyne FLIR Recon long-range, cooled mid-wave infrared (MWIR) thermal systems in remote and austere environments. These systems support law-enforcement missions including suspect detection and identification, detection of small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS), operational overwatch, search-and-rescue, evidence collection, and reconnaissance. The requirement is for a Section 889-compliant, long-range, lightweight thermal system that integrates a low-light visible camera with a cooled MWIR imager and provides a high-definition 1280 � 720 thermal sensor, High Operating Temperature (HOT) MWIR cryo-cooled focal plane array, 8-micron pixel pitch, and 2� doubler lens. The Recon HD also provides long-range detection capabilities, including specified vehicle detection to 9,700 meters and human detection to 3,900 meters. Based on market research, BLM has identified the Teledyne FLIR Recon HD as the only Section 889-compliant solution that meets BLM's requirements for a long-range, high-definition, cooled MWIR thermal binocular/camera system and interfaces with existing field equipment. BLM intends to pursue this acquisition on a sole-source basis under the authority applicable to only one source being reasonably available. Response to Notice All responsible sources may submit a quotation or capability information demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's requirement, which will be considered by the agency. Responses shall be submitted electronically before the end of this announcement period. The Government will consider information received in determining whether a competitive procurement is appropriate.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC) is conducting market research and seeking sources for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Hybrid Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) Single Award Contract; for ARCHITECTURAL-ENGINEER (A/E) services to be conducted worldwide. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541330 � Engineering Services, and the annual size standard is $25,500,000.00. All businesses, including small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owed small businesses, Veteran Owned small businesses, certified HUB-Zone small businesses, certified 8(a) concerns, Woman-Owned Small, and large businesses are encouraged to respond. The information received will be used to formulate the strategy for establishing a set-aside or reserve for small business categories. NAVFAC EXWC anticipates awarding one (1) contract. description: Die Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock, Tiefbauamt, plant den Ersatzneubau der Vorpommernbrücke (BW 102) im Zuge der L 22 über die Warnow. Im Ergebnis einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurde eine Vorzugsvariante entwickelt, die eine Warnowquerung aus 2 Teilbauwerken festlegt. In diesem Zuge sind die Verkehrsanlagen auf dem Bauwerk selbst sowie die auf beiden Seiten vorgelagerten Streckenabschnitte bis zu den Anschlussknoten West und Ost zu planen und zu erneuern. Dabei sind sowohl 2 KFZ- Fahrstreifen stadteinwärts und 2 KFZ- Fahrstreifen stadtauswärts als auch beidseitige Geh- und Radwege zu berücksichtigen. Die vorgesehene Planung der Maßnahme gliedert sich thematisch im Wesentlichen in 3 Teile: 1. die Planung eines neuen Teilbauwerkes Nord (ggf. zzgl. Moorbrücken Nord) mit den entsprechenden verkehrlichen Anbindungen an die benachbarten Knoten, 2. die Planung des Abbruches der Bestandsbauwerke (Vorpommernbrücke, Moorbrücken, Verkehrszeichenbrücke), 3. die Planung eines neuen Teilbauwerkes Süd (ggf. zzgl. Moorbrücken Süd) einschließlich der Planung einer Verkehrszeichenbrücke mit den entsprechenden verkehrlichen Anbindungen an die benachbarten Knoten. Im Rahmen des Vorhabens sind die umweltfachlichen Anforderungen aus Natur-, Arten-, Gewässer-, Boden-, Klima- und Immissionsschutz einschließlich aller daraus resultierenden Genehmigungs- und Nebenbestimmungen zu berücksichtigen.

description: The international research facility FAIR (Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research) is currently under construction at the GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. This project requires numerous different types of detectors for beam diagnostics, including ionization chambers and secondary electron emission monitors. A key component of the design for these detector types is the current-to-frequency converter (IFC), which is used to measure current signals in the nano- and microampere range. The required systems are distributed across the various accelerator facilities on the FAIR campus. Prototype versions of the IFCs have been in use at GSI for some time. As part of this call for proposals, the IFC hardware is to be gradually further developed for the FAIR parameters and, in a second step, produced in series. Aufgrund der Komplexität der Planungsaufgaben, die neben der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung auch architektonische und statische Planungsleistungen erfordern hat sich der Auftraggeber entschieden, die Planungsleistungen an einen Generalplaner zu vergeben. - Umfang: Die Wohnfläche umfasst rund 3.053 m² mit 54 Wohneinheiten. - Projektkosten: Die Kostenschätzung beträgt rund 8.800.000 EUR (brutto) für KG 200-500 u. 700 gem. DIN 276. - Projektdauer: März 2027 bis Mai 2029 - Gegenstand des Auftrages: Generalplanung mit den Leistungen: - Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume (§ 34 HOAI 2021) - Fachplanung Tragwerk (§ 51 HOAI 2021) - Fachplanung Technische Ausrüstung, Anlagengruppen 1- 5 (§ 53 HOAI 2021) - Objektplanung Freianlagen (§ 39 HOAI 2021) - Bauphysik (Wärmeschutz/ Energiebilanzierung und Bauakustik) (Anlage 1 HOAI 2021) - Tiefbauplanung - Brandschutzplanung Der Generalplaner soll unter Berücksichtigung der vorliegenden Planung alle Leistungsphasen gem. HOAI erbringen. Es ist eine Beauftragung in Leistungsabschnitten vorgesehen (Stufe 1: LPH 1-3, Stufe 2: LPH 4, Stufe 3: LPH 5-7, Stufe 4: LPH 8-9). Im Leistungsumfang des Generalplaners enthalten ist auch die vollständige Genehmigungsplanung und Bauantragstellung unabhängig von den Vorschriften der neuen Bauordnung. Der Auftraggeber geht davon aus, dass nachfolgende besondere und sonstige Leistungen erforderlich sind. Der Auftraggeber erwartet vom Auftragnehmer, dass der Auftragnehmer ihn berät und diese Leistungen selbst erbringt oder geeignete Nachunternehmer beauftragt. Besondere und sonstige Leistungen: - Brandschutzplanung (Vorplanung, Entwurfsplanung, prüf- und genehmigungsfähiges Brandschutzkonzept) AHO Heft 17, LPH 1-9 - Energiebedarfsausweis nach Baufertigstellung - Mitwirkung Mieterveranstaltungen - Wohnungsbegehungen mit Mietern - Fördermittelbegleitung projektbegleitend - Abwicklung der Ausschreibungen der einzelnen Gewerke über die e-Vergabeplattform des AGs - Zuarbeiten zur Modernisierungsankündigung und -umlage nach BGB - Baugrunduntersuchung - vollumfängliche Schadstoffuntersuchung ausgewählter Bauteile (Fensterbereich, Dach) - Baustoffliche und Baukonstruktive Untersuchungen (optional) - Bautechnische Untersuchung zur Loggiaverankerung - Begutachtung Loggiaauflager und Brüstungsgeländer - Schallimmissionsprognose, Ermittlung maßgeblicher Außenlärmpegel - Lüftungskonzept Bestand (optional) Der Auftraggeber hat bereits umfangreiche Umbau- und Sanierungsmaßnahmen für den angrenzenden Wohnblock in der Friedrichstraße 10-12a im Jahr 2025 abgeschlossen. In diesem Rahmen wurden bereits Untersuchungen erarbeitet, die den ausgewählten Bewerbern in der Stufe 2 des Verhandlungsverfahrens zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, keinen Projektsteuerer zu beauftragen .

title: Germany – Administration, defence and social security services – 10030260-Appui à la valorisation des potentiels territoriaux pour un développement local inclusif dans le nord du Togo
description: The project "Integrated Territorial Development and Good Governance in Togo" is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). It supports the Government of Togo in advancing decentralisation and territorial development in the regions of Kara and Savanes. Despite progress in decentralisation, regional and local authorities face persistent challenges in exercising transferred competences, delivering quality public services, mobilising local revenues and promoting inclusive local economic development. These constraints are compounded by poverty, climate change, demographic pressure and a fragile security context in northern Togo. The overall objective is to enable regional and local actors to harness the social and economic potential of their territories to improve living conditions in an equitable and sustainable manner. The project applies an integrated territorial development approach with capacity development at individual, organisational and institutional levels. It cooperates with national ministries (Ministry of Local Development, Ministry of Decentralisation, Ministry of Finance), regional councils and municipalities, the National Training Agency for Local Authorities (Agence nationale de formation des collectivités territoriales, ANFCT), the National Association of Municipalities (Faîtière des Communes du Togo, FCT), civil society organisations and private sector actors. To sustain decentralisation and territorialisation efforts, the project also aims at strengthening socio-economic resilience, in particular of communities in the Northen border regions, and provide economic perspectives, in particular for young people. Activities are structured around three complementary outputs: (1) Strengthening the capacities of regional and local authorities to implement transferred competences. (2) Improving collaboration between public institutions, local authorities, civil society and the private sector for inclusive and conflict-sensitive territorial development. (3) Strengthening transparent, participatory and accountable local public financial management. Innovative elements include municipal benchmarking, peer-to-peer learning, digital solutions for local governance, performance-based management and evidence-based decision-making. Gender equality, social inclusion (LNOB), climate resilience, conflict sensitivity and digitalisation are mainstreamed across all interventions to ensure sustainable and scalable results. The assignment targets 38 municipalities in Kara and Savanes through FCT and ANFCT, with a view to progressive replication towards all 117 municipalities. Benchmarking and peer learning will be designed, piloted and institutionalised to steer capacity development and foster continuous improvement. In addition, specialised technical assistance will complement these mechanisms across the three outputs, including support for implementing transferred competences, facilitating inclusive territorial collaboration and strengthening local public financial management (e. g. participatory budgeting, revenue mobilisation, transparency and anti-corruption), while ensuring digital solutions adhere to recognised standards and are interoperable with national ecosystems.
